# 人間向け curated navigation は index.md。本ファイルは AI が grep / 一覧読みするための物。
# Format: <stem>\t<type>\t<path>\t<summary>
# Regenerate: python3 scripts/build_index_txt.py

AGI	concept	concepts/AGI.md	Artificial General Intelligence (AGI) — central to the Technocracy worldview the book positions Plurality against, and a term Plurality replaces with the more grounded "Generative Foundation Models" (GFMs).
Access	concept	concepts/Access.md	Treating broad, equal digital access — bandwidth, devices, literacy, and inclusion in Digital Public Infrastructure — as a fundamental right and precondition for any Plural social order.
Adaptive-Administration	concept	concepts/Adaptive-Administration.md	The use of Generative Foundation Models and other AI tools as adaptive administrative interfaces — capable of bridging cultures, languages, and bureaucratic interfaces — paired with Plural governance to avoid their opacity and bias risks.
Association-and-Plural-Publics	concept	concepts/Association-and-Plural-Publics.md	The protocols and rights for forming groups and "publics" online — federated messaging, end-to-end encryption, secure multi-party computation — so that civil society can exist independently of platform monopolies.
Augmented-Deliberation	concept	concepts/Augmented-Deliberation.md	Using digital tools — bridging algorithms, AI facilitation, broad listening — to scale high-quality deliberation across diversity, beyond the historic trade-off between depth and breadth.
Collaborative-Technology-and-Democracy	concept	concepts/Collaborative-Technology-and-Democracy.md	The book's umbrella framing for Section 5 — technologies that support collaboration across diversity, plotted along a spectrum from deep narrow community to thin broad commodity exchange.
Commerce-and-Trust	concept	concepts/Commerce-and-Trust.md	Quantitative networked trust — community currencies, reputation systems, social-graph-based credit — as a richer substrate for commerce than a universal fungible money.
Connected-Society	concept	concepts/Connected-Society.md	Danielle Allen's vision of a society where bridging ties across lines of difference are formed at a high rate; the normative pillar of the three-part definition of Plurality.
Creative-Collaborations	concept	concepts/Creative-Collaborations.md	Digital tools for co-creation that dissolve barriers of distance, expertise and audience — from open-source software and Wikipedia to AI-assisted "alien art" and the Vesuvius Challenge.
Cybernetics	concept	concepts/Cybernetics.md	Norbert Wiener's transdisciplinary field of control and communication in animals, machines, and society — named briefly in the book as part of the pre-history of the Plural / Connected Society vision.
Data-Coalitions	concept	concepts/Data-Coalitions.md	Organizations that collectively steward and bargain with data on behalf of groups whose interests in that data are inherently shared — modeled on labor unions for the data economy.
Digital-Democracy	concept	concepts/Digital-Democracy.md	Large-scale democracy reimagined as deeply entwined with digital technology, with Taiwan's post-Sunflower civic-tech ecosystem as the leading real-world embodiment.
Digital-Public-Infrastructure	concept	concepts/Digital-Public-Infrastructure.md	Publicly funded, publicly governed digital protocols and services — identity, payments, data exchange — modeled on physical infrastructure and treated as the foundation of a Plural digital economy.
Futarchy	concept	concepts/Futarchy.md	Robin Hanson's proposal — "vote on values, bet on beliefs" — in which policy is chosen by prediction markets that estimate which choice best advances a publicly chosen welfare metric. The book treats it as one mode of Plural Voting.
Generative-Foundation-Models	concept	concepts/Generative-Foundation-Models.md	Large pre-trained AI models (GFMs) such as GPT and BERT — discussed in the book ambivalently as both the most powerful Plural collaborator and as a centralizing technology with severe legitimacy gaps.
Identity-and-Personhood	concept	concepts/Identity-and-Personhood.md	A Plural account of digital identity as intersectional, relational and group-aware — built from verifiable credentials, decentralized identifiers, and the social graph rather than from a single state-issued ID.
Immersive-Shared-Reality	concept	concepts/Immersive-Shared-Reality.md	VR, AR and other multisensory shared environments as a depth-rich form of collaboration across diversity — with serious risks of monopolistic capture, addiction and identity dissolution.
Libertarianism	concept	concepts/Libertarianism.md	One of the two "monist atomism" worldviews — atomistic individuals defended by immutable rights, with markets, cryptography, and "exit" replacing collective politics — that Plurality is positioned against in the book.
Liquid-Democracy	concept	concepts/Liquid-Democracy.md	A voting method in which any voter may delegate their vote(s) to others, who may then re-delegate, allowing bottom-up emergent representation; combined with quadratic rules to avoid power concentration.
Monist-Atomism	concept	concepts/Monist-Atomism.md	The book's umbrella term for the shared metaphysical commitment of Libertarianism and Technocracy — that the world is composed of atomic entities (individuals or a unified whole) governed by a single set of laws — and the primary intellectual foil for Plurality.
Narrow-Corridor	concept	concepts/Narrow-Corridor.md	Acemoglu and Robinson's metaphor for the precarious zone between social collapse and authoritarianism that liberal democracies inhabit — adopted by the book as the frame for technology's twin threats to democracy.
Network-State	concept	concepts/Network-State.md	Balaji Srinivasan's name for internet-native, cryptocurrency-backed, geographically diffuse communities aspiring to territorial sovereignty — named briefly in the book as a canonical Libertarian text.
Plural-Management-Protocol	concept	concepts/Plural-Management-Protocol.md	The community-currency-and-governance protocol used to produce the Plurality book itself — contributors track credits, vote with quadratic methods, and resolve disputes via augmented deliberation, all under a CC0 license.
Plural-Voting	concept	concepts/Plural-Voting.md	The book's umbrella term for voting procedures that go beyond one-person-one-vote — QV, liquid democracy, eigenvoting, predictive voting, and assisted real-time voting — designed to express richer signals of public will.
Plurality	concept	concepts/Plurality.md	Technology for collaboration across social difference, conceived as a third way between Libertarianism and Technocracy and rooted in the Mandarin term 數位 meaning both "digital" and "plural".
Policy	concept	concepts/Policy.md	The Plural alternative to the US, PRC, and EU "digital empires" — a transnational, civil-society-led model of public investment in Digital Public Infrastructure modeled on ARPA / IPTO under Licklider and on Taiwan.
Post-Symbolic-Communication	concept	concepts/Post-Symbolic-Communication.md	The deepest, narrowest end of the depth-breadth collaboration spectrum — brain-to-brain interfaces, telepathic-like sharing that bypasses language and symbol — speculative but treated by the book as a logical extension of Plurality.
Property-and-Contract	concept	concepts/Property-and-Contract.md	Plural protocols for sharing digital assets — storage, computation, and especially data — that decompose the rights to use, alter and profit, and treat data as inherently relational rather than individually owned.
Quadratic-Funding	concept	concepts/Quadratic-Funding.md	A matching-funds formula for public-goods funding in which the matching pool weighs the square root of each contribution and squares the sum, so projects with broad small-donor support get more matching than projects funded by a few large donors.
Quadratic-Voting	concept	concepts/Quadratic-Voting.md	A voting procedure where the cost of casting additional votes on an issue grows quadratically, so voters can express not just direction but intensity of preference while uncoordinated voters do not dominate.
Social-Markets	concept	concepts/Social-Markets.md	Markets redesigned to make space for emergence, group-level effects, and supermodularity — extending capitalism's reach across diversity while overcoming its tendency to crowd out richer modes of cooperation.
Sunflower-Movement	concept	concepts/Sunflower-Movement.md	The 2014 student-led occupation of Taiwan's legislature that catalyzed civic-tech reform, the rise of digital-participation ministers, and the trajectory toward Taiwan's Digital Democracy.
Surveillance-Capitalism	concept	concepts/Surveillance-Capitalism.md	Shoshana Zuboff's term for the political-economy model in which user behavior is the raw material of a new extractive market — quoted as the opening epigraph of the book's chapter 2-0 and referenced throughout the centralizing-threat diagnosis.
Technocracy	concept	concepts/Technocracy.md	One of the two "monist atomism" worldviews — centralized AI-driven optimization of a single welfare function — that Plurality is positioned against in the book.
The-Lost-Dao	concept	concepts/The-Lost-Dao.md	The early Plural vision of the internet associated with J.C.R. Licklider, Doug Engelbart and Ted Nelson — protocols for human–computer symbiosis and intersecting communities that was later eclipsed by private platforms.
Tridemism	concept	concepts/Tridemism.md	Sun Yat-Sen's Three Principles of the People (民族 Mínzú / 民權 Mínquán / 民生 Mínshēng) — civic clan, civic rights, civic livelihood — the founding philosophy of the Republic of China and a deep root of Taiwan's Digital Democracy.
Universal-Basic-Income	concept	concepts/Universal-Basic-Income.md	A periodic cash payment to all citizens — named briefly in the book as a key Technocratic response to AI-driven labor displacement, contrasted with Plurality's collective / supermodular alternatives.
ARPA	entity	entities/ARPA.md	The US Advanced Research Projects Agency and its Information Processing Techniques Office (IPTO) under Licklider — a historical model the book holds up for Plural public investment in transformative digital infrastructure.
Academia-Sinica	entity	entities/Academia-Sinica.md	Taiwan's premier national research institution, named briefly in the book as the institutional base from which Hu Shih shaped post-war Taiwanese education along Deweyan-pragmatist lines.
Andrew-Yang	entity	entities/Andrew-Yang.md	American entrepreneur and politician named briefly in the book as having brought the Technocratic / UBI worldview into mainstream US politics.
Anu-Bradford	entity	entities/Anu-Bradford.md	Columbia legal scholar named briefly in the book as the author of "Digital Empires", whose three-model taxonomy (US / PRC / EU) sets up the book's framing of a fourth Plural / Taiwan model.
Audrey-Tang	entity	entities/Audrey-Tang.md	Co-author of the Plurality book and inaugural Minister of Digital Affairs of Taiwan; identified by the book with the prescriptive component of Plurality and the term 數位.
Ayn-Rand	entity	entities/Ayn-Rand.md	Russian-American novelist and philosopher named briefly in the book as a foundational fiction-side influence on contemporary Libertarianism.
Balaji-Srinivasan	entity	entities/Balaji-Srinivasan.md	Technologist and author of "The Network State" (2022) named briefly in the book as a canonical exponent of the contemporary Libertarian / cryptocurrency-secessionist worldview.
Cass-Sunstein	entity	entities/Cass-Sunstein.md	Harvard legal scholar named briefly in the book as the author of "#Republic", whose diagnosis of filter-bubble polarization motivates the chapter on bridging algorithms.
Charles-Dodgson	entity	entities/Charles-Dodgson.md	19th-century Oxford mathematician — better known as Lewis Carroll — named briefly in the book as the originator of the multi-vote weighting question that leads to Liquid Democracy and Quadratic Voting.
Chiang-Kai-Shek	entity	entities/Chiang-Kai-Shek.md	Leader of the Republic of China who relocated to Taiwan in 1949 — named briefly in the book as the figure whose Rural Land Reform and Article-145 cooperative policies turned Tridemism's Mínshēng principle into Taiwan's economic foundation.
Curtis-Yarvin	entity	entities/Curtis-Yarvin.md	Software engineer and political writer (pen name "Mencius Moldbug") named briefly in the book as a canonical author of the contemporary Libertarian / neo-reactionary current.
Danielle-Allen	entity	entities/Danielle-Allen.md	Political philosopher whose "Connected Society" / "Justice by Means of Democracy" supplies the normative pillar of the book's three-part definition of Plurality.
Daron-Acemoglu	entity	entities/Daron-Acemoglu.md	MIT economist named briefly in the book as the co-author of "The Narrow Corridor" (with James Robinson) and "Power and Progress" (with Simon Johnson), whose framings supply key building blocks for the book's diagnosis.
Doug-Engelbart	entity	entities/Doug-Engelbart.md	Engineer of networked, collaborative computing named briefly in the book as one of the three Lost Dao figures alongside Licklider and Ted Nelson.
Elon-Musk	entity	entities/Elon-Musk.md	Entrepreneur and OpenAI co-founder named briefly in the book as a Silicon Valley exponent of the Technocratic AGI worldview.
Georg-Simmel	entity	entities/Georg-Simmel.md	German sociologist named briefly in the book as "one of the founders of sociology" whose idea of the "web" critiqued the individualist concept of identity — a precursor to Connected Society.
Gitcoin	entity	entities/Gitcoin.md	The leading platform for Quadratic Funding rounds, channeling over $100M to public-goods projects — and the platform that helped fund the production of the Plurality book itself.
Glen-Weyl	entity	entities/Glen-Weyl.md	Co-author of the Plurality book; founder of RadicalxChange, Microsoft Research's Plural Technology Collaboratory and the Plurality Institute; co-author of Radical Markets; inventor of modern Quadratic Voting.
Hannah-Arendt	entity	entities/Hannah-Arendt.md	Philosopher whose 1958 book The Human Condition supplies the descriptive component of the book's three-part definition of Plurality — that the human condition is plurality, the fact that men, not Man, inhabit the world.
Henry-George	entity	entities/Henry-George.md	19th-century American political economist named briefly in the book as a key source for Tridemism's Mínshēng principle and for Taiwan's later land-value tax and cooperative-enterprise policy.
Hu-Shih	entity	entities/Hu-Shih.md	Chinese philosopher and reformer named briefly in the book as Dewey's student, translator of pragmatism in China, and a central influence on Taiwan's educational tradition.
Iain-M-Banks	entity	entities/Iain-M-Banks.md	Scottish science-fiction novelist named briefly in the book as a fictional source of the Technocratic superintelligence vision, via the Culture series.
Isaac-Asimov	entity	entities/Isaac-Asimov.md	American science-fiction author named briefly in the book as a foundational fictional source of the Technocratic vision of superintelligence.
JCR-Licklider	entity	entities/JCR-Licklider.md	J.C.R. "Lick" Licklider — psychologist and computer scientist whose 1960s ARPA / IPTO vision of human–computer symbiosis and the "Intergalactic Computer Network" is the book's "Lost Dao" of Plurality.
Jaclyn-Tsai	entity	entities/Jaclyn-Tsai.md	Taiwanese lawyer and Minister Without Portfolio named briefly in the book as one of the world's first ministers for digital participation — and the figure who recruited Audrey Tang into Taiwan's government.
James-Robinson	entity	entities/James-Robinson.md	Political scientist and economist named briefly in the book as the co-author (with Daron Acemoglu) of "The Narrow Corridor", source of the book's framing metaphor for liberty under technological pressure.
John-Dewey	entity	entities/John-Dewey.md	American pragmatist philosopher named briefly in the book as a deep intellectual root of Taiwan's Digital Democracy via his Chinese student Hu Shih.
John-Perry-Barlow	entity	entities/John-Perry-Barlow.md	Cyber-libertarian poet and EFF co-founder named briefly in the book as the author of the 1990s "Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace" — a peak articulation of Libertarianism.
Join	entity	entities/Join.md	Taiwan's official government petition and consultation platform, complementing vTaiwan and embodying the book's vision of Digital Democracy at scale.
Lionel-Penrose	entity	entities/Lionel-Penrose.md	British psychiatrist and mathematical geneticist named briefly in the book as the originator (1946) of the square-root rule that underpins Quadratic Voting.
Marc-Andreessen	entity	entities/Marc-Andreessen.md	Venture capitalist and Netscape co-founder named briefly in the book as the author of the 2023 "Techno-Optimist Manifesto" — quoted as one of the two epigraphs to chapter 2-0.
Mark-Granovetter	entity	entities/Mark-Granovetter.md	Stanford sociologist named briefly in the book as "the leading figure of network sociology" — whose work supplies the social-theory foundation for the Plural / Connected-Society view.
Neal-Stephenson	entity	entities/Neal-Stephenson.md	American science-fiction novelist named briefly in the book as the source of "Snow Crash"'s metaverse and a primary fictional influence on contemporary Libertarianism.
Nick-Bostrom	entity	entities/Nick-Bostrom.md	Philosopher of existential risk named briefly in the book as a key exponent of the Technocratic AGI worldview.
Norbert-Wiener	entity	entities/Norbert-Wiener.md	MIT mathematician named briefly in the book as the coiner of "cybernetics" and a pioneer who perceived the limits of modernity even as he helped construct it.
Peter-Thiel	entity	entities/Peter-Thiel.md	Silicon Valley venture capitalist named briefly in the book as the central intellectual leader of the Libertarian / Network State worldview that Plurality positions itself against.
RadicalxChange	entity	entities/RadicalxChange.md	The non-profit organization founded by Glen Weyl that advances Plurality-aligned mechanism design including quadratic voting, quadratic funding, and quadratic liquid democracy.
Ray-Kurzweil	entity	entities/Ray-Kurzweil.md	Inventor and futurist named briefly in the book among the science-fiction-adjacent Technocratic visionaries whose "predictive futurism" of superintelligence the book positions Plurality against.
Reid-Hoffman	entity	entities/Reid-Hoffman.md	LinkedIn co-founder and venture capitalist named briefly in the book as Sam Altman's mentor and a leading Silicon Valley exponent of the Technocratic AGI worldview.
Robin-Hanson	entity	entities/Robin-Hanson.md	George Mason economist named briefly in the book as the originator of Futarchy — "vote on values, bet on beliefs" — one of the Plural Voting extensions discussed in chapter 5-6.
Sam-Altman	entity	entities/Sam-Altman.md	OpenAI co-founder and CEO named briefly in the book as a leading exponent of the Technocratic / AGI-centered vision of the future.
Shoshana-Zuboff	entity	entities/Shoshana-Zuboff.md	Harvard Business School professor emerita whose "Age of Surveillance Capitalism" is quoted as the book's opening epigraph for chapter 2-0.
Sun-Yat-Sen	entity	entities/Sun-Yat-Sen.md	Founder of the Republic of China and architect of Tridemism (Three Principles of the People), treated by the book as a foundational figure in the genealogy of Taiwan's Digital Democracy.
Ted-Nelson	entity	entities/Ted-Nelson.md	Hypertext pioneer named briefly in the book as one of the three Lost Dao figures and the inventor of Project Xanadu's two-way bidirectional links and micropayments.
g0v	entity	entities/g0v.md	Taiwan's open-source civic-tech community ("gov-zero") that builds shadow versions of government services and underpins much of Taiwan's Digital Democracy ecosystem.
vTaiwan	entity	entities/vTaiwan.md	Taiwan's civic-tech consultation platform using Pol.is and structured deliberation to surface rough consensus across cleavages on policy issues.
plurality-book	source	sources/plurality-book.md	The 2024 CC0 book by E. Glen Weyl, Audrey Tang and the Plurality community articulating Plurality as the future of collaborative technology and democracy.
